connection_type: I'm an interested observer — no direct personal connection
disclosure_text: I live in Florida, so I have meet lots of friends who are immigrants or decedents of them so I feel somewhat strongly when I hear lots of negative things about them.
micronarrative:
I've always been pretty supportive of immigrants, but I feel a bit disconnected from both the pro-immigrant and anti-immigrant groups. On one hand, I believe in having strong borders and enforcing the law, but on the other, I think the path to citizenship should be streamlined and easy for those who have been here for a while. I find myself feeling out of place in both camps, even though I disagree more with the anti-immigrant stance. So, I tend to keep my head down and avoid getting too involved.

I also think it’s a good policy to not let people into the country as citizens if they have committed felonies in their home country. There could be rare exceptions, but it would be a much harder process. I try to balance my personal beliefs with compassion. I can’t really think of a situation where supporting strong borders and being compassionate towards immigrants would come into conflict. If someone does something wrong, they should be punished, whether it’s through a fine or just being put at the bottom of a list.
